scenarios.description: Two parallel trajectories remain well outside the synthetic horizontal threshold.
Nominal trajectories converge at the same altitude; the conservative envelope flags conflict before the crossing.
Horizontally coincident trajectories remain outside the synthetic vertical threshold.
Uncertainty envelopes trigger a planning conflict even though nominal horizontal distance exceeds the base threshold.
A fast relative crossing occurs between sample times; the velocity-based conservative expansion catches it.
Coordinates with different reference-frame identities must not be compared as if they shared a frame.
An unqualified clock basis cannot support authoritative space-time comparison.
An intent whose validity ends before the simulation window ends is rejected as stale.
An emergency-priority intent with no synthetic conflict still requires a competent-authority review.
The same numeric timestamps in unrelated epochs cannot be compared as a common space-time plan.
A withdrawn intent cannot be treated as current future traffic.
